To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the fixed point of Bellman operator can be used as a global objective for inverse Reinforcement Learning, (b) the fixed point is well-defined for a large class of cost functions and (c) the fixed point can be approximated using the same techniques as in classical RL.
the Bellman optimisation operator is a natural and more general way to characterise the optimal policy in IRL, and that the resulting algorithm is more robust and scalable.

1) the classical approach to IRL is sub-optimal, 2) a new formulation of IRL as an optimization problem is introduced, 3) a novel algorithm is derived, and 4) a new theoretical framework for analysing the performance of IRL algorithms is developed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: how can one estimate the fixed point of a Bellman operator from a finite set of trajectories?
the following questions: (i) How to define a notion of optimality for the inverse problem that does not induce an explicit bias against long term planning?
developing a generalised inverse reinforcement learning framework that can be used for a wide class of optimality criteria.

the current IRL framework is too restrictive.
the IRL framework is not well suited to solve the problem of learning the reward function.

the classical IRL objective is not well suited to estimate a cost function that would lead to optimal trajectories in the classical sense.

IRL is a generalised inverse problem that can be cast as a convex optimisation problem with a non-convex regulariser, and that the classical IRL objective can be seen as a specialisation of the latter.
